title: 19th Annual Pershing Square Value Investing and Philanthropy Challenge
description: 19th Annual Pershing Square Value Investing and Philanthropy Challenge
summary: The speaker argues that Baker Hughes is undergoing a fundamental transformation into a high-quality industrial energy infrastructure platform, driven by electrification and data center demand, which the market currently underestimates. Regarding Monster Beverage, the speaker contends that Celsius Energy is undervalued relative to Monster due to superior growth and margin expansion potential, while noting Monster's struggles in the sugar-free category. The analysis also touches on the competitive landscape for delivery services, suggesting Door Dash has a singular focus advantage over Uber and Tesla in the short-to-medium term.
thesis: The speaker argues that Baker Hughes is undergoing a fundamental transformation into a high-quality industrial energy infrastructure platform, driven by electrification and data center demand, which the market currently underestimates. Regarding Monster Beverage, the speaker contends that Celsius Energy is undervalued relative to Monster due to superior growth and margin expansion potential, while noting Monster's struggles in the sugar-free category. The analysis also touches on the competitive landscape for delivery services, suggesting Door Dash has a singular focus advantage over Uber and Tesla in the short-to-medium term.

claims.claim: The speaker identifies Baker Hughes as a utility company with significant grid capacity additions driven by electrification, noting its utility segment is larger than data centers.
claims.quote: And this this page really shows it uh where I think the the light blue uh line really shows that trend take off and power is is that segment uh of utilities that's is is bigger than even data centers for a company like Baker Keys

claims.claim: The speaker argues the market is undervaluing Celsius Energy's growth potential and believes the company can exceed market standards by 400 basis points in the medium-term.
claims.quote: Celsius Energy is the third largest energy drink company in the US today after Red Bull and Monster. It has two main brands, Celsius and Alan. The market today is undervaluing its growth potential and we believe that we can exceed growth by the market standards by 400 bips in the medium-term

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Celsius trades at a forward PE multiple lower than Monster despite having higher forward growth estimates and earnings.
claims.quote: The forward PE multiples show a similar story with Celsius today being available at a price lower than that of Monster despite having the same forward earnings as per estimates

claims.claim: The speaker states that Monster is losing market share in the sugar-free category and lacks the DNA to innovate like Celsius and Alani.
claims.quote: Number one, in Sugarfly today, Celsius is number one because of the Celsius and the Alani blend together. They've already beaten Monster and Monster is in fact losing share.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates that Celsius will achieve 250 basis points of operating margin expansion in the medium-term.
claims.quote: And we believe 250 bills in the medium-term is achievable coming to valuation today Celsius trades at a sales multiple lower than the industry median as well as companies such as Q Dr. pepper, Coca-Cola, and Monster Beverages

claims.claim: The speaker identifies an asymmetric long opportunity in Baker Hughes with significant upside potential driven by energy infrastructure buildout and a shift toward industrial energy technology.
claims.quote: We have found that this has created an asymmetric long opportunity in Baker Hughes with three 63% upside potential over the next three years. Our work has found that the market underappreciates the role Baker Hughes plays in the energy value chain
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker forecasts that Baker Hughes's revenue will shift significantly toward industrial energy technology, transforming the business into a compounder with higher quality earnings.
claims.quote: Our work has found that by 2028 over 60% of this business's revenue will come from industrial energy technology. This transforms Baker Hughes into a business that will increasingly look like a seaman's energy or a G Vernova instead of a Hallebertton or a slumber.
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker argues that LLMs cannot replace GDS systems due to high inference costs, insufficient uptime, and small revenue pools, making AMD's API infrastructure essential.
claims.quote: So fundamentally as it stands today, LMS cannot replace the GDS. And lastly, we think about revenue pools. Here we have OpenAI and Anthropic competing in or have revenue pools of about $45 billion. Similarly, the largest OTAAS have a revenue pool of $65 billion and GDS's have a mere $6 billion.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions Microsoft (implied by 'OpenAI') and Anthropic as competitors with large revenue pools, but notes they prefer the larger OTAAS revenue opportunity over the smaller GDS one.
claims.quote: Here we have OpenAI and Anthropic competing in or have revenue pools of about $45 billion. Similarly, the largest OTAAS have a revenue pool of $65 billion and GDS's have a mere $6 billion. So when we see these large LMs, we see them performing at the top of the funnel
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker believes Baker Hughes is undergoing a fundamental business transformation that the market is underestimating, leading to significant margin expansion and a shift to a service-based revenue model.
claims.quote: We believe the market is underestimating the compounding effect of this dynamic. These two factors are driving a fundamental shift in the business model and we believe that Baker is now at an inflection point that the market is underestimating.
claims.speaker: null

claims.claim: The speaker believes Baker Hughes is transitioning into an industrial energy infrastructure platform, with IT revenue rising from 40% to over 50% in just the last three years.
claims.quote: Baker's transitioning into an industrial energy infrastructure platform as IT has risen from 40% to over 50% of this revenue in just the last 3 years alone. And through the combination of increased infrastructure demand and expansion of services, we believe this trend to continue into the next several years.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Baker Hughes is worth more as a combined entity due to synergies in manufacturing complex turbo machinery components and sourcing raw materials, rather than splitting the businesses.
